prompt: Write 10 distinct lessons the claims-triage agent (home and motor claims assessment within delegated authority) at Larkmere Mutual learned across many cases about: worried the house is in a flood zone. Each is a working pattern or tip for the next case, not about any one member, one or two sentences, in the agent's voice ("When…, …"). Return {"items": [{"type": "fact" | "preference" | "observation", "content": "..."}]} with exactly 10 items. (batch 0)
response: {"items":[{"type":"observation","content":"When a member says they are worried the house is in a flood zone, I check the exact property location against the latest flood mapping before I comment, because nearby roads and postcodes can have very different risk levels."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the concern is about flooding, I separate river, coastal and surface-water risk rather than treating them as one issue, because the likely cause and next steps can differ."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the member mentions recent heavy rain or blocked drains, I treat surface water as a live possibility even if the property has never flooded before, because first-time flooding often follows exceptional weather."},{"type":"preference","content":"When I can give a clear, plain-English explanation of what the flood check shows, I do so early, because uncertainty about risk tends to be the main cause of anxiety."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the property is not in a high-risk flood area, I still ask about local signs such as nearby watercourses, previous overland flow, or repeated garden pooling, because local history can matter more than the broad postcode view."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the member is worried but no flood damage has occurred, I avoid using alarmist language and instead focus on practical precautions, because reassurance is part of good triage."},{"type":"observation","content":"When flood risk is uncertain, I look for evidence of recent mitigation such as raised thresholds, airbrick covers or drainage work, because those details can reduce both likelihood and severity."},{"type":"preference","content":"When the claim involves possible flooding during a storm, I check whether wind-driven rain or blocked external drains may be the real issue, because the best next question depends on how water entered the home."},{"type":"observation","content":"When a member believes being near a river automatically means the house is in a flood zone, I correct that gently, because proximity alone does not tell me whether the property is at material risk."},{"type":"fact","content":"When I am deciding whether a flood
